title: A circle draws a sine wave
summary: A horizontal guide carries the point’s height from the unit circle to the plot. Sage paper and quiet axes let the growing copper trace lead the eye.
rules: Composition: Keep the explanation on the left and the diagram on the right. Align the unit circle’s center with the plot’s zero line at y = 196 within the SVG.
Color and line: Use sage for the paper, dark green for type and the radius, and copper for projected height and the wave. A dashed guide distinguishes the construction from the solid result.
Motion: Copy the circle point’s height directly across while the angle advances to the right. Keep previous heights as a continuous trace and complete one turn at 14.2 seconds.
Static view: Use the completed wave as the poster. Keep 0, 2π, and ±1 legible and let the viewer start the animation when ready.

palette.label: Quiet guide for the untraced curve

mainImage.alt: A point on the unit circle and the end of a partial sine wave are connected by a horizontal dashed line.
mainImage.caption: 7.6 s · The two marks share one height; the dashed line makes the mapping visible before the wave is complete.

staticImage.alt: The unit circle and a complete sine wave share a zero line. The plot marks 0, 2π, +1, and −1.
staticImage.caption: 17 s · The complete period and its axis labels remain visible after the rotation stops.
